bear.narrative: The store machine slows and the cash runs out before the fixed cost base does. Same-store sales turn negative as a crowded Indonesian coffee market absorbs the 100-outlet year and discounting returns, so revenue growth lands 8pp below base in every year and the 2026 expansion becomes over-capacity: gross margin gives back 1.5pp on coffee and dairy bought under contracts that no longer look cheap, the operating cost ratio rises 2pp because rent and store payroll do not flex with the ticket count, and the truncated rollout has to be completed at a higher cost per outlet, adding 2pp to capex intensity. With free cash flow after rent already negative in 2026, that mix is what forces the funding event: a slower rollout first, then a discounted placement into a 21% float if the leases still have to be paid. Tax, payout and terminal growth are the base case's.

bull.narrative: The unit economics compound and the capital intensity falls. Same-store sales stay positive alongside the store programme, so revenue growth runs 8pp above base in every year; the donut format and the central kitchen lift food attachment and hold gross margin 1.5pp higher, and the operating cost ratio falls 2pp as store density covers the head-office and central-kitchen base more than we assume. The fourth shock is the asset-light path the report identifies: converting part of the company-operated estate to a franchise or landlord-funded fit-out, and the central kitchen supplying food to more outlets per rupiah of capex, cuts 2pp from capex intensity and lifts the return on the capital the company keeps. Tax, payout and terminal growth are the base case's.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +50.0% is the company's own guide, not our caution: management told the May 2026 public expose to expect top line growth of about 50% [S3 p.4], and the nine months are running slightly ahead of it at +53.3% on 9M2025's Rp1,041.8bn [S4 p.61]. We take the guide rather than the run-rate because the fourth quarter carries the strongest comparator of the year (Q4 2025 was Rp455.4bn, the first quarter shaped by the 2025 estate), so +50% for the year is the most probable outcome and +53% would need the fourth quarter to outgrow the first nine months. The lower net profit growth in our build (+52% against the +70% bottom-line guide [S3 p.4]) is not a haircut: the nine-month net profit itself grew 49.7% [S4 p.7] because tax normalised to 27.4% from almost nil a year earlier, and the guide needs a fourth-quarter acceleration the reported nine months do not show. FY2027E +26.0% then fades to +13% by FY2030E: growth is store-led - 322 outlets, 100 more planned for 2026 [S2 p.20][S3 p.4] - and revenue per average outlet is rising only modestly, so the model cannot rely on same-store acceleration to hold a 40% rate. The long-run rate is 5.0%, below Indonesian nominal GDP growth in our macro deck, because a coffee chain with a 3-5 year store lease book [S4] matures faster than the economy it sells into.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the recorded rate, not shaded. FY2025 gross margin was 61.74% and 9M2026 61.68% [S2 p.8][S4 p.6] - cost of sales grew 53.7% against 53.3% revenue growth, so the mix of beverages (89.8% of FY2025 sales) and food has been margin-neutral [S2 p.85]. Management has price locks and annual contracts in place through 2026 and states it has no plan to raise menu prices this year despite vendor requests [S3 p.3], which is why no expansion is assumed; the long-run 61.0% allows a small give-back as food and donut sales (9.8% of FY2025 revenue and growing) carry a lower gross margin than beverages [S2 p.85].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Set to zero. The company's disclosed input cost pressure comes from coffee, dairy and packaging bought under annual contracts and price locks [S3 p.2-3], none of which is a series in the agricultural deck we own (cpo, soyoil, wheat, corn, soymeal). No share of COGS is mechanically linked to a deck driver, so nothing is compounded through the engine.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Set to zero together with link1_share: there is no linked cost base to pass through, and management has explicitly said it does not intend to raise menu prices in 2026 [S3 p.3].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Set to zero for the same reason as link1: the second deck channel is the wheat and soy complex, which reaches Fore only through pastry and donut inputs, a small share of a 9.8% food segment [S2 p.85]. Disclosed in section 2 rather than modelled.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Set to zero with link2_share. No deck-linked cost base and no planned price increase for 2026 means there is no pass-through to model [S3 p.3].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The line now charges the store rent as an operating cost, so the model's EBITDA is struck after rent and every scenario pays the rent its own revenue implies. The recorded 9M2026 operating expense ratio was 53.46% of sales against 55.51% a year earlier [S4 p.6], and the FY2025 ratio was 54.68% [S2 p.96]; those reported ratios carry right-of-use depreciation but not the lease payments, which Indonesian filers put in financing. We take the reported ratio, remove the right-of-use depreciation of 104.5bn (6.98% of FY2025 revenue) and charge the lease payments instead - 152.1bn in the nine months to September 2026 on 1,597.2bn of sales, 9.53% [S4 p.9] - so the wedge added to every year is 2.55pp and the rent the LK books below the line now sits in operating cost [S2 p.41][S4 p.9]. The underlying ratio still eases from the 9M actual to 54.9% by FY2030E as store density rises, the same operating-leverage story as before; every new outlet adds its rent to this line, which is why the charge grows with the estate rather than being a fixed number in a valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 5.42%, the owned-asset charge only. FY2025 D&A was Rp187.7bn, of which right-of-use depreciation was Rp104.5bn (6.98% of revenue) and fixed-asset depreciation Rp88.2bn (5.89%) [S2 p.41][S2 p.44]. The right-of-use charge is removed here because the lease payments themselves are now charged in opex_pct: keeping both would deduct the same lease twice, and adding back right-of-use depreciation in the FCFF formula while the rent leaves as cash would credit a non-cash charge that the rent already covers. Store depreciation is spread over 4-8 year lives and the lease book over 3-5 years, so both grow with the store count, which is the same driver as revenue.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is store-led, so we build it from the outlets rather than fade a ratio. FY2026E 11.2% is the company's own budget of about Rp250bn [S3 p.3] on our Rp2,246bn revenue, which is about Rp2.5bn per net new outlet on the 100 planned [S3 p.4]; FY2025 is the calibration - Rp191.7bn of additions on 90 net new outlets [S2 p.251][S2 p.20], about Rp2.1bn per store and 12.8% of revenue. Carrying that per-store cost against the net additions implied by our revenue path (100 in 2026, then a step down toward the 2025 pace as growth fades) gives a glide from 11.2% to 8.5% by FY2030E and 7.2% in the long run. The long-run rate is the depreciation of the owned fixed assets (Rp88.2bn on FY2025 sales, 5.9%) plus growth capex for the stores a 5% terminal growth rate still requires; the ratio falls because store growth falls, not because the estate gets cheaper to fit out. The 5.89% owned-asset depreciation is the replacement anchor, and the right-of-use depreciation that used to sit alongside it is not a capex charge at all - the rent that funds it is charged in opex_pct on every outlet the revenue path implies, existing and planned, so no part of the leased estate is valued as rent-free.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Negative, as recorded: -6.2% of sales at the end of FY2025 and -4.6% at 30 September 2026 [S0][S4], because stores collect cash at the counter while suppliers, landlords' fit-out contractors and accrued staff costs are paid on terms. Held at -4.6%, the latest actual, so no working-capital release is credited to the forecast as the business grows.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The 9M2026 accounts show the real burden: Rp34.032bn of tax on Rp124.039bn of pre-tax profit, 27.4% [S4 p.6], against 13.0% for FY2025 and a near-nil charge in FY2024 when accumulated losses shielded profit [S2 p.8]. FY2026E 26.0% lets the fourth quarter come in slightly below the nine-month rate as the deferred tax asset is used, and the long-run 24.0% sits above the 22% statutory rate for the part of costs (employee benefits, some marketing) that is not deductible.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 7.4%, the bank-borrowing rate, now that the interest line carries bank debt only. FY2025 finance cost was Rp14.556bn, of which Rp11.1bn was lease interest [S0][S2 p.41]; the remaining Rp3.456bn is bank interest on opening bank debt of Rp46.757bn (opening total debt of Rp217.672bn less the Rp170.915bn lease liability at 31 December 2024), which is 7.39%. That is the rate the engine now applies to a debt line that excludes lease liabilities: lease interest is not charged here any more because the lease payments, interest included, are charged as rent in operating costs [S4 p.9].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 3.5%, reset from the engine's 6.7% average: 9M2026 interest income of Rp6.965bn on an average cash balance of roughly Rp260bn is about 3.5% annualised [S4 p.6][S4 p.9], and the Bank Indonesia policy rate in our macro deck is 5.75%, so deposit rates cannot be much higher.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has been repaying bank loans (Rp8.182bn in 9M2026) and funding expansion from operating cash flow and the IPO proceeds [S4 p.9]; the lease book grows with the store count and is inside the debt balance and the right-of-use asset, not new gross borrowing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The other income and expense lines in 9M2026 net to Rp-7.176bn and are dominated by finance cost and interest income, both modelled explicitly [S4 p.6].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the group is wholly owned below the listed parent, and there is no minority interest on the balance sheet at 30 September 2026 [S4].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero for the forecast and for the long run. The AGM resolved that no dividend can be paid this year because accumulated losses are still negative - Rp87.790bn at 30 September 2026 after the nine-month profit [S3 p.3][S4 p.8] - and the company has never paid one. Until that account is positive, all earnings stay in the business.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. 8,918,359,270 shares were listed on 14 April 2025 after the IPO of 1.88bn new shares at Rp188 [S2 p.11-12], and no further issue, buyback or split is announced [S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 5.0%, below Indonesian nominal GDP growth in our macro deck (the deck carries real GDP growth of 5.29% and CPI of 3.28% for FY2027E, so nominal growth of roughly 8.6%) because a store network matures to replacement capex and category-level same-store growth; it is at the top of what a restaurant estate can sustain without unit-count growth, and it is paired with terminal capex that covers the depreciation of the owned fixed assets even though it sits below total D&A, because most of that D&A is right-of-use depreciation matched by rent rather than by our capex. The line is a house assumption from the macro deck, not a company disclosure.

challenges.challenge: The FCFF formula (model lines: ebit*(1-a.tax_rate)+da-capex-delta_nwc) adds back all D&A, including ROU depreciation of 104.5bn in FY2025 (F6), but never deducts lease payments of 149.9bn (F20, 10.0% of revenue). FY2025 actual OCF 316.9 - capex 191.7 - lease payments 149.9 = -24.7bn, against the model's +119.5bn FCFF; FY2026E FCFF is +170.5bn before ~221.6bn of rent. The DCF therefore values the 322-store leased estate as rent-free.
challenges.answer: The FCFF is pre-lease by construction and the report now says so. The rent on the estate trading at the valuation date is capitalised in valuation.bridge (-2746: nine-month lease payments annualised, grown at 4.5%, discounted at the WACC, less the 269.6 lease liability already in net debt), and section 4 reconciles FY2025A: model FCFF of 119.5 against OCF less capex less lease payments at [S2 p.251]. DCF now 438 a share, base value 336, HOLD.

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is run on the model's net_debt line, which is net cash of 279.6 in FY2026E and 918.1 in FY2028E only because lease payments are never deducted. It prints 10.2x FY2026E and 7.4x FY2027E 'entry' multiples against an actual Sep-2026 net debt of 44.4 (10.9x FY2026E). The implied exit multiple is also not shown: TV 9,968.3 / terminal EBITDA 1,169.8 = 8.5x, not 'roughly today's FY2026E entry multiple' (10.2x claimed, 10.9x actual).
challenges.answer: The entry multiple is now built from published components - market cap, cash of [S4], lease liabilities of [S4] and FY2026E EBITDA - not the forecast net cash line, which section 3 labels an artifact of the pre-lease accounting. The exit multiple is stated as terminal value over terminal EBITDA and as below the entry multiple but above the peer median in the table. EV/EBITDA weight cut to zero for this reason.

challenges.challenge: Capex falls from 11.2% of revenue in FY2026E to 8.0% by FY2035E (input capex_pct 0.112/0.080), but the same model grows revenue 16% in FY2029E, 13% in FY2030E and 5% to FY2035E with revenue per outlet flat, so the growth is store-led and needs fit-out capex. The drift.capex_pct justification cites only the 2026 Rp250bn budget (which supports 11.2%, not 8.0%) and asserts the estate matures while the forecast triples revenue.
challenges.answer: Capex path re-derived and sourced: 2026 budget of Rp250bn for 100 outlets [S3 p.3-4], FY2025 actual Rp191.7bn for 90 net adds or about Rp2bn per outlet [S2 p.251][S2 p.20], and a fade to 8.5% by 2030 with a terminal 7.2% that covers owned D&A plus growth capex. The drift justification carries the per-outlet arithmetic; the holding-11.2% case is discussed in the sensitivity text.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue growth of 47.8% (2,212.8) is below the company's public guide of about +50% at the 11 May 2026 expose [S3 p.4] and below the 9M2026 run-rate of +53.3%. The build implies Q4 2026 growth of about +35% against Q4 2025's 455.4, and no source is given for that deceleration. Net profit growth of +48.9% is 21pp below management's +70% guide.
challenges.answer: FY2026E growth raised to the company guide of about +50% [S3 p.4], above the 9M run-rate fade and consistent with [S4 p.61]. We do not take the +70% net profit guide and the report gives the reason: the tax charge normalised to the statutory rate in 2026 from almost nil in 2025, so nine-month net profit grew 49.7% while operating income grew faster [S4 p.6-7].

challenges.challenge: The ADD rating is carried by the bull tail. Base-case value today is 531, below the 555 price; the target 684 is 47% composed of the 25%-weighted bull at 1,280 (bull contributes 320 of 684). Re-weighting to base 40/bear 50/bull 10 gives 499, a -10% return, below the price: the conclusion does not survive the bear probability being doubled, which is the checklist test.
challenges.answer: Rating moved to HOLD off the base case rather than the tail: base value 336 and tp_base 375 are both below the 555 price, with the scenario-weighted 516 only clearing the price through the bull quarter. The bull probability stays 25% as the mirror of a 25% bear with 50% base, but the rating no longer depends on it; section 4 prints the base case stand-alone.

challenges.challenge: The printed cost-of-capital build does not reproduce its own output: 7.45% rf + 0.887 beta x (4.23% ERP + 2.46% CRP) = 13.4%, not the printed 11.77% COE. The engine silently deducts a 1.62pp sovereign spread (7.45 - 1.62 = 5.83% before beta), which is not disclosed, so a reader applying the stated inputs lands outside the 11-13% house band.
challenges.answer: The sovereign-spread deduction is now disclosed and the formula printed line by line: (7.45% - 1.62%) + 0.887 x (4.23% + 2.46%) = 11.77% cost of equity, WACC 11.53%. Section 4 explains why the spread is deducted - the rupiah yield already embeds default risk that the country premium would charge twice - and points to the sensitivity grid for the band. No company filing is cited for these inputs, which are house macro-deck ones.

challenges.challenge: The report prints an insider register of 84.9% and a free float of 21.1% in the same sentence (and again in sections 5 and 6): the two sum to 106%. The datapack's insider_pct (84.92, Yahoo/S0) conflicts with S2 p.67, which shows Fore Holdings 78.917%, Otten 0.002% and public 21.080% of 8,918,359,270 shares.
challenges.answer: Insider ownership restated to 78.92% from the company register [S2 p.67] and held as fact F24; the 84.9% data-pack figure is named, described as irreconcilable with the float, and dropped in sections 1, 5 and 6. The free float stays 21.08%, so the two now sum to the share capital.

challenges.challenge: Claims about the model itself are cited to the company's annual report: the target roll-forward and probability weighting (summary, 'gives Rp684 [S2]'), the scenario design ('nothing else changes in either [S2]', s5), the cost of capital ('inside the house band [S2][S0]'), and terminal growth 5.0% ('[S0]', Yahoo Finance). [S2] cannot support any of them and [S0] cannot support a growth assumption.
challenges.answer: Model construction no longer cites the annual report. The scenario design and probability weighting are described as house method, the cost of capital is labelled the house macro-deck build, and terminal growth is linked to the macro deck with GDP 5.29% and CPI 3.28% in the assumption basis. [S2] is now used only for company facts and [S0] only for market and peer data.

challenges.challenge: Funding risk is absent. On a lease-adjusted basis 9M2026 free cash flow is about -30bn (OCF 279.7 - capex 190.7 - rent roughly 120) and FY2027E capex is 281.6bn before rent, yet the report says 'the growth is funded' and 'the balance sheet is liquid'. There is no bear case for a discounted placement or rights issue, which would also hit the 21% float.
challenges.answer: Funding stress added as a first-class risk: nine-month operating cash flow less capex less lease payments is negative [S4 p.9], cash fell from 327.5 to 233.2 [S4 p.4], and the bear narrative now runs through the placement into a 21% float. The capital allocation paragraph says reinvestment is funded by IPO proceeds as well as operations, replacing the claim that the growth is self-funded.

challenges.challenge: The report calls multiple de-rating 'the strongest argument against the target', but the bear case shocks only revenue growth, gross margin and opex; the 30% multiple weight stays at the base-case values in both bear and bull. The one risk the report ranks highest is therefore not in the scenario set at all.
challenges.answer: The engine applies scenario shocks to operating inputs only, so a multiple shock cannot be attached to the bear case without overriding the peer multiple, which would import a price view into every period; the de-rating is instead quantified as the P/E cross-check at the peer median of 9.6x, worth Rp97 a share and carrying 30% of the blend, which section 4 now prints as the de-rated outcome. The report no longer ranks de-rating highest without showing its value.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is only three mirrored operating shocks. It excludes the two upside paths the report itself identifies: conversion of company-operated stores to a franchise/asset-light model (which would change capital intensity and ROIIC) and a successful donut/central-kitchen food attachment, plus the float/index catalyst. Management's +70% net profit guide is above even the bull's starting point.
challenges.answer: A fourth mirrored shock added: capex_pct plus two points in the bear (a truncated rollout costs more per outlet) and minus two in the bull, where the saving is the asset-light path - franchise or landlord-funded fit-out with the central kitchen supplying more outlets per rupiah. The donut and food-attachment path is in the bull narrative at the gross-margin and opex shocks, and the float sell-down is a dated catalyst.

challenges.challenge: The D&A paragraph double-counts: 88.2bn owned depreciation (F5) plus 104.5bn ROU depreciation (F6) sums to 192.7bn, but the model and the summary use 187.7bn (12.5% of revenue) and the summary says 'Rp187.7bn, of which 105 was ROU', implying owned depreciation of 82.7bn, not 88.2bn.
challenges.answer: Reconciled and stated once: the notes give 88.2 owned plus 104.5 right-of-use, and the pack line of 187.7 is 5.0 lower because that slice of owned depreciation is charged inside cost of sales [S2 p.44]. The model uses the pack line for internal consistency and section 3 says the economic charge is the sum; the summary no longer implies owned depreciation of 82.7.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 20.62% is 1.03pp above FY2025A's 19.59% and is not answered in qc_justifications (only drift.capex_pct is). The weights.changed WARN (70/20/10 against the 60/30/10 industry default) is also unjustified in qc, although the report gives a rationale in prose.
challenges.answer: The 1.03pp EBITDA margin step-up is explained in section 3: the nine-month operating margin of 8.2% [S4 p.6] carried through a fourth quarter at the same cost ratio, with gross margin stable and depreciation growing with the estate; the gap is inside the engine calibration tolerance. weights.changed is justified in qc_justifications with the trailing-versus-growth argument and [S2 p.20][S4 p.61].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 renders the data-breach size squared: "affecting about 5.7 million accounts million customer accounts". F27 already carries the unit "million accounts" and the prose adds a second unit on top, so the one place the report sizes the incident is garbled.
challenges.answer: F27 carried a phrase as its unit (million accounts) and the sentence added million customer accounts on top; the unit is now million and the prose reads about 5.7 million customer accounts. The quote and S5 are unchanged.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states that 22.0% is "the tax rate used in the model". The model runs a.tax_rate of 26.0% in FY2026E easing to 24.0%, and 22.0% appears only as the tax input to the WACC shield. A reader auditing the tax shield or the FCFF is given the wrong rate.
challenges.answer: The 22.0% is now labelled the WACC shield input, and the P&L rate the model runs is printed beside it: 26.0% in FY2026E easing to 24.0% from FY2029E, which are the rates inside the FCFF and the earnings [S4].

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is asserted, not printed. Section 4 says the terminal value is "below the multiple the shares carry today on the same post-rent basis" and never gives the number, on an initiation whose SELL is a 48.6x forward-earnings call.
challenges.answer: Both ends are now printed on the undiscounted basis: terminal value built from FY2035E FCFF grown at g and capitalised at WACC less g against FY2035E EBITDA and EBIT (low single digit on EBITDA, high single digit on EBIT), versus the 18.7x entry multiple, stated as under a quarter of entry. The engine exposes no terminal-multiple placeholder, so the ratio itself is given as its components plus that fraction rather than as a typed number.

challenges.challenge: The card discipline g = reinvestment x ROIIC is never stated, so the 5.0% terminal growth cannot be tested against the post-rent return it is claimed to sit below. A SELL on a 40x multiple needs that arithmetic in the open.
challenges.answer: The identity is stated: g = reinvestment rate x ROIIC. Terminal capex of 7.2% against 5.4% owned depreciation leaves net reinvestment of about a third of after-tax EBIT, implying an ROIIC in the mid-teens against the 11.5% WACC, with the near-year return around thirty per cent fading to that terminal figure [S2][S4].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case shocks only revenue growth, gross margin and opex; it omits the franchise/asset-light conversion the report itself names as a capital-intensity change, the float/index catalyst, and management's +70% FY2026 net profit guidance, which is 21pp above the model's +49%.

missing_bear_case.note: No bear case for funding: on a lease-adjusted basis 9M2026 free cash flow is about -30bn (OCF 279.7 - capex 190.7 - rent ~120), yet the report says growth is funded. No rights-issue/placement stress and no de-rating shock, although de-rating is called the strongest argument against the target.

assumption_realism.note: The cash-flow assumptions are not realistic on leases: the model charges no rent although FY2025 lease payments were 10.0% of revenue, and capex fades from 11.2% to 8.0% while revenue still grows 13-16% to FY2030 and revenue per outlet is flat. Both are value drivers, not second-order items.

evidence_and_citations.note: The 84.9% insider figure (Yahoo datapack) contradicts S2 p.67 (Fore Holdings 78.917%, Otten 0.002%, public 21.080%) and cannot coexist with a 21.1% float. Model construction claims (target weighting, scenario mirroring, cost of capital) are cited to [S2], the annual report, which cannot support them.

valuation_method_fit.note: Fatally, the compounder DCF is built on FCFF = EBIT(1-t) + D&A - capex - dNWC, which adds back ROU depreciation but never deducts lease payments, so the leased estate is valued as rent-free; the terminal value also assumes 5% growth with capex below D&A. Cost-of-capital inputs as printed do not reproduce the 11.8% COE.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary's claim that gross margin and store productivity are the two things that move value omits the dominant issue (rent). The base-case value of 531 is below the 555 price; the 684 target is 47% dependent on the 25% bull tail and falls to 499, below the price, if the bear weight is doubled.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck linkage is correctly zeroed: green coffee, dairy and packaging are not in the agricultural deck, and the report describes the currency channel rather than inventing a link. Macro deck inputs (USD/IDR, BI rate) are used consistently.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservatism runs the wrong way here. FY2026E revenue growth of 47.8% is below the company's own ~50% guide [S3 p.4] and below the 9M run-rate of +53.3%, implying an unsourced Q4 deceleration to ~+35%; net profit +48.9% versus +70% guided. Meanwhile the capex fade and free-rent treatment are unjustified optimism that moves value far more.

calibration.note: The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 20.62% is 1.03pp above FY2025A's 19.59% and has no qc_justification; the weights.changed WARN is also unjustified in qc_justifications. Neither is a BLOCK, but both drift the base year away from the last actual without a cited reason.

signoff.notes: Round 2 signoff - APPROVED with notes. The call and the construct are accepted: SELL, target Rp286 against Rp555, base case Rp185, and the lease correction (rent in operating cost, owned depreciation only, lease liability out of net debt, same treatment in all three scenarios) is internally consistent and reconciles to the filing [S4: 9M2026 OCF 279.7 less capex 190.7 less lease payments 152.1 is negative]. I am not re-arguing any of it. The three open auditor items are recorded here and quantified because each is real, and each cuts AGAINST the analyst own SELL, so none flatters the call or changes the rating; that is why they do not carry a return, not because they are correct. Q9 (FIX, unanswered): da_pct 5.42% does not reproduce from its own cited basis - the basis text itself quotes Rp88.2bn of fixed-asset depreciation on Rp1,497.1bn = 5.89%, and pack D&A less ROU = 5.56% - and no source for 5.42% is given, so the input is an unsourced departure from the LK in the direction that understates value. Effect as audited: DCF 195 to about 214, target 286 to about 294 (total return -47.0%), still SELL. The record therefore carries the corrected figure; the rating and direction stand either way, and the published target is about 3% conservative, well inside the scenario-weighted noise of a 33-743 range. Q9 stays owed on the analyst file. Q10 (FIX, unanswered): section 4 twice labels pre-tax EBIT as after-tax - the text says after-tax EBIT of Rp338.2bn taxed at 24.0%, and after-tax EBIT of Rp177.0bn against Rp127.4bn. The model EBIT lines are 177.0 (FY2027E) and 338.2 (FY2035E); the after-tax equivalents are 134.5 and 257.0. The ROIIC results (mid-teens terminal, about 30% near term against an 11.5% WACC) are unchanged because they were computed off the after-tax delta; only the labels are wrong, and the corrected pair is printed here so the ROIIC arithmetic can be audited from this record. Q11 (NOTE, unanswered): the claim that revenue per average outlet rose only modestly holds on year-end counts (4.65 vs 4.48, +3.8%, F1/F7) but not on an average-count basis (nearer +12%); and the claim that the economic EBITDA is less than half the reported figure is wrong at 53.8% (249.1 against pre-rent 463.1), i.e. about half. Both are text-only and both narrow, not widen, the claimed gap. Desk pattern note for the analyst: three items in one report (Q10/Q11 plus the round-1 L1/L2 mislabels) are all text_vs_numbers on a valuation section a -48% SELL invites readers to audit line by line; the house will not keep accepting corrected text in the record as a substitute for correct text in the report on future initiations. Publisher note: Q9/Q10/Q11 are known and quantified here; if the text is edited before release, use the figures in this note and rerun nothing else. Batch: FORE is the only FOOD_BEVERAGE name at signoff tonight and the desk other live names (ROTI.JK, DLTA.JK) are still at red team, so there is no batch to bias-check; the method-weight deviation (70/30/0, EV/EBITDA zeroed because peer EBITDA is pre-rent and ours post-rent) is justified on the WARN and accepted. No broker rating, target or consensus was used or seen.

bias.note: Revenue is the company guide of about +50% for 2026 [S3 p.4] on the 322-outlet estate [S2 p.20], not a haircut; gross margin 61.7% [S2 p.8][S4 p.6], opex 56.0% (9M2026 53.46% less right-of-use depreciation 7.1% [S4 p.47] plus rent 9.53% [S4 p.9]) and capex 11.2% on the Rp250bn budget [S3 p.3] all reproduce from the last actual and the plan. The two identifiable departures sit on the conservative side and are quantified: terminal g of 5.0% is derived from g = reinvestment x ROIIC on terminal capex of 7.2% against owned depreciation of 5.4%, and the da add-back at 5.42% is about 0.5pp under its sourced basis (finding Q9). Closing both takes the DCF to about 214 and the target to about 294, still -47% against the 555 price: the call does not rest on caution. Scenarios mirror the same four drivers (+/-8pp growth, +/-1.5pp gross margin, -/+2pp opex, -/+2pp capex) at 25/50/25, base above 40%.

recomputed.item: Net debt / (net cash) at 30 Sep 2026 (Rp bn), leases excluded because rent is charged in opex
Outlets at end-2025 (volume driver) against the 2026 plan of 100
Owned D&A as % of FY2025 revenue used by the model

findings.finding: da_pct of 5.42% does not reproduce from its own cited basis: F5 puts FY2025 fixed-asset depreciation at Rp88.2bn on revenue of Rp1,497.1bn, which is 5.89%, and the as-filed pack D&A less right-of-use depreciation (187.7 minus 104.5) is 5.56%. The input basis text quotes 5.89% and s3 writes 5.4%, so the EBITDA add-back is 0.14 to 0.47pp of revenue below the owned charge embedded in opex_pct.

s4 labels pre-tax EBIT as after-tax EBIT twice: after-tax EBIT of Rp177.0bn against Rp127.4bn the year before, and after-tax EBIT of Rp338.2bn taxed at 24.0%. The model ebit line is 177.0 for FY2027E and 338.2 for FY2035E; the after-tax figures are 134.5 and 257.0. The quoted ROIIC of about 30% and mid-teens is reproducible only from the after-tax delta, so as printed a reader cannot tie the sentence to the arithmetic.

The extreme_call justification says revenue per average outlet has risen only modestly: on year-end counts it is +3.8% (4.65 against 4.48), which supports the sentence, but the average-outlet basis is nearer +12% and no 2023 outlet count is held in facts. The same paragraph says the economic EBITDA is less than half the reported figure, when 249.1 against the pre-rent 463.1 on the same revenue is 53.8%.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -8.5pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The minus 8.5pp move is the rent, not a change in unit economics. FY2025A is the filed EBITDA, struck before lease payments, which Indonesian filers report in financing [S2 p.251]; from FY2026E the model charges the lease payments themselves in operating cost and adds back only the owned-asset depreciation of an equivalent 5.42% of revenue, so EBITDA falls by the rent net of the right-of-use charge. At FY2025A revenue the same treatment gives the filed EBITDA of Rp293.5bn less the Rp149.9bn of lease payments paid that year, so the FY+1 margin reproduces the last actual's economics on the corrected basis rather than drifting below them [S2 p.41][S4 p.9]. Every scenario pays rent at the same ratio to its own revenue, so the correction is not a forecast-specific haircut.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -4.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex is built from the outlets, not faded from a ratio, and the path is 11.2% (FY2026E), 10.8%, 10.0%, 9.2%, 8.5% (FY2030E) and 7.2% from FY2031E - the engine applies the long-run rate from the sixth year rather than fading to it, so there is no 8.6% intermediate year. FY2026E is the company's Rp250bn budget on our Rp2,246bn of revenue, about Rp2.5bn per net new outlet on the 100 planned [S3 p.3-4]; FY2025 was Rp191.7bn of additions on 90 net openings, about Rp2.1bn per store [S2 p.251][S2 p.20]. The revenue path at flat revenue per outlet implies about 422 outlets at end-2026 and about 1,070 by FY2035E, so the net additions it implies are about 100 a year in 2026-28 and about 45-50 a year in 2031-35. From FY2031E the line is therefore mostly replacement of a ~1,000-store estate: replacement at the FY2025 owned depreciation rate of 5.9% of revenue is Rp316-335bn, plus 45-50 new stores at Rp2.1-2.5bn is Rp95-125bn, i.e. 7.2-8.1% of revenue. The 7.2% endpoint (Rp409bn in FY2035E) is at the bottom of that band; we hold it because revenue per outlet rises as stores mature, making the FY2025 replacement rate an upper bound on the mature estate, and because capex is still above the owned depreciation it replaces.

flags.message: debt FY2025A restated at 0.07x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's FY2025 debt of Rp218.1bn includes the Rp201.9bn lease liability [S2 p.41], which the model no longer treats as debt: the lease payments that service it are charged in operating cost in every forecast year, so carrying the liability as borrowed money as well would deduct the same obligation twice. We restate debt to the long-term bank loan of Rp16.2bn that the notes disclose for 31 December 2025, which with the Rp201.9bn lease liability reconciles exactly to the pack's Rp218.1bn [S4 p.55].

flags.message: balance-sheet debt restated at 0.03x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's 30 September debt includes the Rp269.6bn lease liability [S4 p.46], and the valuation net debt must exclude it because the rent that pays for it is now inside FCFF; including both would charge the lease twice. We restate the balance-sheet debt to the Rp8.0bn long-term bank loan disclosed at 30 September 2026, which with Rp269.6bn of lease liabilities reconciles to the pack total, so the equity value is struck after the lease once [S4 p.55][S4 p.46].

flags.message: expected return -48%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is produced by three sourced drivers, and none of them is a valuation input. First, rent: lease payments are 9.53% of revenue (Rp152.1bn in nine months of 2026 on Rp1,597.2bn of sales) and sit in financing, so a corporate FCFF built on the filed statements never pays the landlord; we charge them in operating cost on every outlet the revenue path adds, which is what turns the base-case economic EBITDA to less than half the reported figure and leaves FY2026E FCFF negative [S4][S2]. Second, capex: the company's own 2026 budget is Rp250bn, 11.2% of our revenue forecast, and the long-run ratio is 7.2%, so rent and capex together absorb most of the EBITDA the stores throw off [S3][S2]. Third, revenue per outlet: the company does not disclose same-store sales and revenue per average outlet has risen only modestly while the estate grew from 232 to 322 outlets, so the store count does the work and the post-rent cash-flow value is a small fraction of the price [S2][S4]. The reverse DCF is printed in the report: the price implies revenue growth several points above our path in every forecast year, which is what the reverse solve returns; the call is therefore priced off the operating arithmetic the filings report, not off a target multiple. With 30% of the blend on the peer P/E of 9.6x forward earnings the implied value is lower still, so both methods point the same way [S0].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.1}
flags.justification: The weights are 70% DCF, 30% P/E and zero for EV/EBITDA, a deliberate deviation from the industry default 60/30/10. EV/EBITDA is zeroed because our EBITDA is now struck after the rent while the peer enterprise-value multiples are struck before it, so the two sides are on different accounting bases unless the multiple is computed on EBITDAR, which the peer set does not report [S2][S4]. The DCF takes seven tenths because it is the only method that reaches the store build and charges the rent every scenario's estate requires; the P/E keeps three tenths because it is an equity method - net income already carries the lease, with the rent in operating cost and the lease interest no longer a separate charge, so the earnings number and the equity value both sit after the obligation [S4].
